description:
Redwood Inference is formalizing a reliability program that makes availability/latency/error expectations explicit by product tier (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity) and ties operational behavior to error budgets. The project “Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy” will (1) define tier-specific SLOs for key customer journeys (chat/completions streaming, embeddings, model catalog operations, and dedicated pool readiness), (2) standardize indicators and measurement windows across regions/models/routes, and (3) implement enforcement mechanisms so teams “feel” error budget burn via release gates, progressive rollouts, and automatic mitigation (graceful degradation, fallbacks, and throttling) rather than only post-incident learning.

Goals:
- Establish a single, company-wide source of truth for SLOs per tier (Hosted vs Dedicated), including clear definitions of SLIs (success rate, 5xx rate, timeouts, streaming disconnect rate, p95/p99 latency) and what’s excluded (customer-side timeouts, misuse, invalid auth, etc.).
- Define an error budget policy: burn-rate thresholds, alerting, escalation, and what happens when budgets are at risk or exhausted (change freezes, canary-only, feature flag constraints, increased approval requirements).
- Implement enforcement in tooling: CI/release checks, canary analysis that consults current error budget, and routing controls that prefer safe fallbacks when burn spikes.
- Reduce incident volume and MTTR by making “budget burn” a leading indicator and improving runbooks and automation.

Scope:
- In scope: Hosted API + Dedicated tiers (tiered SLO tables; dashboards; alerting; release gating; routing degradation policies; postmortem templates updated to reference budget burn; status-page comms triggers).
- Partial scope: Private deployments (documented mapping guidance and optional targets, but no enforcement gates initially due to customer-managed environments).
- Out of scope: Commercial SLA contract changes (handled separately); major architecture rework of the runtime.

Key stakeholders:
- SRE leadership/owners: Sean Gallagher (SRE Director), Rafael Mendes (SRE Manager), Aisha Bello (SRE).
- Platform/control plane & routing: Priya Natarajan (VP Eng Platform), Ethan Park (EM Control Plane), Mina Haddad (EM Smart Routing), Ravi Menon (Staff Routing), Jordan Lee (Policy Engine).
- Product: Lauren Bishop (Dir PM Dedicated), Marissa Cole (Dir PM Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (SPM Rollouts).
- Partner teams: Telemetry/observability (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman), API Gateway (Amara Diallo), Customer Support/Success for escalation alignment.

Timeline (hypothetical, realistic for Redwood scale):
- Phase 0 (2–3 weeks): Baseline current reliability, inventory existing metrics/dashboards, draft SLO proposals, align on tier principles.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): Publish SLO definitions, implement SLI calculations and dashboards, wire burn-rate alerting.
- Phase 2 (4–8 weeks): Implement enforcement: rollout gates, change management policy, canary automation, and routing degradation rules.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): Tune thresholds, reduce noise, incorporate learnings from incidents and customer escalations.

Constraints & considerations:
- Metrics correctness/cardinality (per-model/per-route/per-region) must be controlled.
- Dedicated tier SLOs must reflect pool isolation and capacity commitments; Hosted SLOs must reflect multi-tenant behavior and broader model mix.
- Enforcement must be gradual (start with “warn-only” gates and a pilot set of services) to avoid blocking urgent fixes.

Primary deliverables:
- Confluence SLO spec + error budget policy + enforcement playbook.
- Linear project plan with engineering/PM tasks.
- GitHub PRs across redwood (control plane, routing, gateway), observability-pack, perf-canary, slo-toolkit, incident-bot.
- Slack coordination threads, incident-related discussions, and announcements.
- Support tickets that motivated tier differentiation and “what to communicate when budgets burn.”

files.description: Canonical SLO table and definitions per tier: SLIs, targets, measurement windows, per-endpoint breakdown (chat/completions streaming vs non-streaming, embeddings), region/model dimensions, and explicit exclusions.

Error budget policy: burn rate thresholds, paging vs ticketing, escalation paths, what changes when budgets are at risk/exhausted (release gates, approvals, change freeze), and how to request exceptions.
Detailed SLI calculation spec: how to count successes/failures, classify timeouts, streaming disconnect taxonomy, and mapping of HTTP/gRPC codes to error classes; includes examples and edge cases.
Dedicated-specific SLO considerations: pool readiness, cold-start behavior, autoscaling lag, noisy-neighbor isolation, and how to measure per-customer dedicated SLOs without leaking data.
Dashboard conventions for SLOs: folder structure, naming, required panels, standardized filters (tier/region/model/route), and links to runbooks and error budget policy.
Organization-wide standard for burn-rate alerts: recommended multi-window burn alerts, sensitivity by tier, anti-flap guidance, and required annotations (owner, runbook, mitigation).
ADR documenting the decision to implement tier-aware SLOs and error-budget-based enforcement, alternatives considered (single global SLO, per-model SLO only), and migration plan.
Runbook for when a service/tier is near/exhausted budget: checklist, mitigation actions (throttling, routing fallback, feature flag rollback), comms guidance, and who to page.
When and how to communicate customer-facing impacts related to budget burn: status page triggers, Dedicated vs Hosted messaging templates, and coordination with Support/CS.
How-to for engineers: integrating budget checks into CI/CD and rollout tooling; warn-only vs block modes; override procedure; examples for runtime, gateway, and routing services.
Product requirements for the initiative: user stories (SRE, oncall, PM, enterprise customers), reporting needs in Console, and success metrics (incident reduction, fewer regressions).
Design spec for Console surfacing: error budget remaining, burn forecasts, change history overlays, and rollout guardrails; includes MVP vs future roadmap.
Working notes from kickoff: current pain points, initial SLO strawman, open questions (streaming disconnects, per-model variance), and assigned owners.
Draft queries and validation steps comparing logs vs metrics for SLIs; notes on sampling, cardinality, and known data quality issues.
Pilot rollout plan for enforcement: which services participate first, stages (warn-only → soft block → hard block), and rollback/override criteria.
PM analysis mapping existing Dedicated commitments to proposed SLOs, gaps vs current performance, and suggested customer messaging.
Dataset snapshot used to propose targets: historical latency/error distributions by tier/region/model; includes methodology notes.
Proposal for metric labels and cardinality controls to support tier/model/route breakdowns without exploding storage or query cost.
Diff-style notes describing how oncall procedures will change with error budgets (new alerts, new escalation triggers, new mitigations).
Early product thinking/wire notes for Console integration: what to show, permissions, and how to present tier context.
Cross-functional kickoff meeting transcript (SRE, Platform, Product): goals, tier principles, ownership, and timeline alignment.
Review meeting transcript focusing on policy enforcement and exception handling; debate on block vs warn-only and Dedicated-specific nuances.
Meeting transcript between PM Console/Rollouts and engineering on how to wire budgets into canary analysis and UI.

PM ticket: finalize tier principles and customer-facing narratives; ensure Dedicated positioning aligns with operational reality.
